nodes.title: SG-10.2.2 Scene applies the store's focusedObjectId as hover highlight and label
nodes.body:
Context: gameStore already exposes focusedObjectId and setFocusedObject (game/frontend/src/store/gameStore.ts). SceneObject already has focus() and blur() that show the same highlight and label as hover. BootScene.onStateChange (game/frontend/src/phaser/BootScene.ts) only calls sync(state) on each object and never reads focusedObjectId. Desired behavior: on every store change the scene focuses the object whose spec.id equals focusedObjectId and blurs all others, and clears focus on all objects when the value is null. Expected result: setting the store focus highlights and labels the matching object, and null clears them. Why: keyboard focus pushed into the store must be visible in the canvas.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given focusedObjectId is set to an existing visible object id, When the store changes, Then BootScene calls focus() on that SceneObject and blur() on every other focused object
- Given focusedObjectId is null, When the store changes, Then no SceneObject is focused and focused objects are blurred
- A unit test with Phaser mocked asserts both the highlight and label path (focus) and the clearing path (blur)


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene.onStateChange reading focusedObjectId
- In scope: Unit tests with Phaser mocked
- Out of scope: Writing focusedObjectId from the keyboard handler
- Out of scope: Changes to gameStore
- Out of scope: Changes to SceneObject rendering
- Preserve: Existing sync(state) calls
- Preserve: focusChange and menuClose emissions
- Preserve: SHUTDOWN cleanup


## Technical constraints
- Reuse SceneObject.focus() and blur(); do not add a second highlight path
- Phaser 3.90 mocked in tests via vi.mock('phaser')


## Definition of done
- Both requirements have passing unit tests
- No regression in existing bootScene*.test.ts suites


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Scene focuses the object matching the store focusedObjectId
nodes.body:
Context: onStateChange only syncs objects. Desired behavior: read focusedObjectId from the game store and call focus() on the SceneObject whose spec.id matches, blurring non-matching focused objects. Expected result: the matching object shows highlight and label. Why: shared focus state must be visible in the scene.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given focusedObjectId equals an object's spec.id, When onStateChange runs, Then that object's focus() is called once
- Given another object is focused and focusedObjectId names a different object, When onStateChange runs, Then the other object's blur() is called
- Given focusedObjectId names no scene object, When onStateChange runs, Then no object receives focus() and nothing throws


## Scope
- In scope: BootScene.applyFocusedObject
- Out of scope: Null clearing branch
- Preserve: sync(state) behavior


## Technical constraints
- Do not call setFocusedObject from the scene to avoid store loops


## Definition of done
- Matching object focused on store change


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: REQ · Scene clears focus on all objects when focusedObjectId is null
nodes.body:
Context: after focus was applied, the store may reset focusedObjectId to null (for example menu close). Desired behavior: BootScene blurs every focused SceneObject when the value is null. Expected result: no object keeps highlight or label. Why: stale highlights must not remain.

## Acceptance criteria
- Given a focused object and focusedObjectId changes to null, When onStateChange runs, Then blur() is called on that object
- Given focusedObjectId is null and no object is focused, When onStateChange runs, Then no blur() call is made and nothing throws


## Scope
- In scope: Null branch of applyFocusedObject
- Out of scope: Keyboard-initiated focus
- Preserve: Existing keyboard focus behavior in onKeyDown


## Technical constraints
- Use SceneObject.isFocused to decide whether to blur


## Definition of done
- Null store focus clears scene focus


## Clarifying questions
- None

nodes.title: Act: Add applyFocusedObject to BootScene and call it from onStateChange
nodes.body:

- onStateChange reads useGameStore.getState().focusedObjectId and passes it to applyFocusedObject
- Matching object gets focus(); other focused objects get blur()

- Out of scope: gameStore changes
- Preserve: sync(state) loop

- Code path: `game/frontend/src/phaser/BootScene.ts`

- Method wired in onStateChange
